finding.title: Delete or wire up dead code kept alive only by its own tests: ContentResult and CalendarCycleDao's legacy methods
finding.why: grep for ContentResult/ContentLoaded/ContentNotFound outside content_result.dart finds only test/story_acceptance/epic_19_offline_first_test.dart, which constructs and pattern-matches the type in isolation — no repository, service, or provider in lib/ ever returns or consumes a ContentResult; the content DAOs in this same batch (text_cache_dao.dart, daily_content_dao.dart) return plain nullable Future<T?> instead, exactly the shape ContentResult looks built to replace per EH-2's 'convert to a value at the data-layer boundary'. Likewise getCycleForProgramAndDate/getCyclesForDate/getCyclesForDateRange in calendar_cycle_dao.dart have zero callers anywhere in lib/ (grep confirms) — only content_database_comprehensive_test.dart's 'legacy method ... delegates' tests call them. In both cases a green test suite hides that the code has no real consumer; deleting either wouldn't be caught by any user-facing behavior change, only by the tests written specifically to keep them alive.
finding.recommendation: Delete ContentResult/ContentLoaded/ContentNotFound and its test, or wire it into the content DAOs' return types if the EH-2 result-type pattern is actually wanted there. Delete calendar_cycle_dao.dart's 3 legacy methods and their delegate tests, or confirm via a repo-wide symbol search that nothing external depends on them before the next release.
acceptance_criteria: grep for ContentResult/ContentLoaded/ContentNotFound and for getCycleForProgramAndDate/getCyclesForDate/getCyclesForDateRange outside their own definition+test either returns a real production call site, or the symbols are deleted.

finding.title: Extract the duplicated _extractFirebaseCode regex parser out of MagicLinkService and UpgradeToCloudService
finding.rule: Fowler: duplicated code; layering tension with Rule 3
finding.why: Both files independently reimplement 'parse a Firebase error code out of an exception's toString()' via the identical regex, because Rule 3 blocks these features/account/{domain,data} files from importing FirebaseAuthException directly and matching its typed .code field. The fallback is fragile: if a Firebase Auth SDK bump changes the exception's string format so it no longer wraps the code in literal brackets, _extractFirebaseCode silently returns null everywhere at once — in upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart this means the 'email-already-in-use' retry-merge branch falls through to rethrow, and the guided merge flow silently stops firing, surfacing a raw exception to the user instead. The same helper is also duplicated at 3 more sites repo-wide (signup_screen.dart, sign_in_controller.dart, upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart), confirming this is a systemic gap rather than a one-off.
finding.recommendation: Factor the regex parser into one shared, unit-tested helper (e.g. core/utils/firebase_error_code.dart, which only touches strings so it doesn't trip Rule 3) that all current call sites import.
acceptance_criteria: one shared, unit-tested extractFirebaseCode(Object e) utility exists
magic_link_service.dart and upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart delegate to it instead of each defining their own regex copy

finding.title: Delete or replace compile-time-tautological assertions across Epic 1/2 acceptance tests
finding.why: In null-safe Dart, `expect(SomeClass, isNotNull)` on a Type literal, a non-nullable getter, or a non-nullable top-level provider constant is guaranteed true by the type system before the test ever runs — the same is true for a bare `expect(true, isTrue)`. None of these 42 assertions, spread across 6 of Epic 1's 12 stories (1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 1.9) and 3 of Epic 2's AC blocks, can fail for any runtime reason; they only prove the referenced symbol resolves at compile time, which flutter analyze / the test file's own import block already guarantees. Story 1.3, for example, consists of exactly these two assertions and nothing else, yet the file header claims 'All 12 stories are DONE and actively tested,' and CLAUDE.md frames `make test-story-X.Y` passing as the story's acceptance gate ('always validate it before marking it done'). A regression in AuthGuard's guard logic, AppRouter's routes, SyncOrchestrator's wiring, or any of the 11 DAOs' real behavior ships green through that gate.
finding.recommendation: For each site, either delete the assertion (documenting that the import block is the only intended check) or replace it with a behavioral assertion that calls a representative method/route/guard and checks its actual return value — the pattern Stories 1.2, 1.6, 1.11, 1.12 and the rest of Epic 2 already use in the same files.
acceptance_criteria: No `expect(X, isNotNull)` remains where X's static type is non-nullable, and no standalone `expect(true, isTrue)` remains, in epic_01_foundation_test.dart / epic_02_content_test.dart
Each surviving test in the affected groups exercises at least one real method call or return value

finding.title: Move codecs_and_mergers_test.dart's two suites to their AG-5-mirrored paths under test/core/sync/codec/ and test/core/sync/merge/

evidence.quote: ///   - [UiPreferencesMerger] LWW gate, per-field writes, cross-profile isolation,

finding.why: This one file tests two unrelated source files — lib/core/sync/codec/stage_definition_codec.dart and lib/core/sync/merge/ui_preferences_merger.dart — at neither of their AG-5-mirrored paths. test/core/sync/codec/ doesn't exist at all despite lib/core/sync/codec/ holding 15 codec files; test/core/sync/merge/ already exists (mergers_test.dart, drift_merge_store_test.dart) but doesn't hold ui_preferences_merger_test.dart either. The repo additionally carries a second, non-mirroring test/sync/ tree (test/sync/merge/*_roundtrip_test.dart, test/sync/codec_rules_contract_test.dart) that also touches stage_definition_codec.dart at a different (DB-integration) layer, so an agent grepping for 'where is the StageDefinitionCodec test' has to check three locations before finding this one.
finding.recommendation: Split into test/core/sync/codec/stage_definition_codec_test.dart and test/core/sync/merge/ui_preferences_merger_test.dart, each mirroring its lib/ counterpart 1:1.
acceptance_criteria: stage_definition_codec_test.dart exists at test/core/sync/codec/ and ui_preferences_merger_test.dart exists at test/core/sync/merge/

finding.title: Delete or merge stale learning_screen_test.dart into learning_screen_l1_test.dart

evidence.quote:
// With no active curricula, the empty state is shown
      expect(find.text('No active tracks'), findsOneWidget);

finding.why: learning_screen_test.dart overrides dashboardActiveCurriculaProvider and dashboardUserModeProvider (lines 19-27) — I grepped learning_screen.dart's ref.watch calls and confirmed it reads neither provider; both overrides are dead, left over from before the screen was refactored onto dashboardActiveCurriculaStreamProvider/coarse-track providers. Its 'renders without error' and 'shows key UI elements' tests are a strict, weaker subset of learning_screen_l1_test.dart's empty-state tests (same setup, same assertion, less specific). Only the AppErrorView regression test (lines 70-93) is unique, and it doesn't exercise LearningScreen at all. Net effect: a second file that must be kept in sync with LearningScreen's provider surface for zero incremental protection, and it's currently out of sync (see the DB-leak finding above, which independently proves this).
finding.recommendation: Move the unique AppErrorView regression test to a location that actually reflects what it tests (e.g. a core/widgets AppErrorView test, or leave in learning_screen_test.dart renamed), delete the two redundant/stale tests and dead overrides, and remove learning_screen_test.dart per TQ-7 with the reason stated in the commit message.
acceptance_criteria: learning_screen_test.dart is deleted or contains only the non-duplicate AppErrorView test
No override in the remaining file references a provider LearningScreen does not read (grep ref.watch in learning_screen.dart against the override list)
